correctness.rationale: Conditioning on Y gives the observed standardized covariance score \(S=(\delta R+Z)/\sqrt{1+\delta^2}\), while each null-resampled standardized score is iid N(0,1). Conditional exceedance counts are therefore binomial and give the exact finite-n, finite-B power integral and exact null size. Under \(\delta=h/\sqrt n\), \(R/\sqrt n\to1\) yields the fixed-B local limit. On the exact-size subsequence the rejection threshold is a beta order statistic; a Taylor expansion at its mean yields the displayed negative \(1/B\) coefficient. Independent numerical evaluation reproduced the quoted h=2, alpha=.05 powers and coefficient.

originality.rationale: The most directly relevant CRT power paper explicitly separates the empirical finite-resample cutoff from its analytical power calculation and states that its power results cover empirical resampling only when the number of resamples diverges. Generic Monte Carlo randomization-test literature establishes rank corrections and studies simulation budgets, but no inspected result supplied this Gaussian marginal-covariance finite-n power integral or the explicit local \(1/B\) loss coefficient. The final claim therefore resolves a concrete finite-resampling question not implied by the inspected CRT asymptotics.
